elements.quote: Cancer is a complex, multilevel phenomenon [1-5] in which health outcomes depend on highly interrelated elements across stages of etiology, prevention, screening, diagnosis, treatment, survivorship, and end-of-life care [6, 7]. Standard bench and clinical research approaches alone are not well suited to account for this complexity... The extent to which system dynamics modeling has been applied specifically to cancer prevention and control has not been studied.
elements.reason: The Introduction describes the current state of knowledge on system dynamics in public health and identifies the key uncertainty/gap: the application to cancer prevention and control has not been studied.

elements.quote: To overcome persistent barriers to providing high-quality, equitable care, approaches are needed to address this complexity and provide guidance for successful intervention... The extent to which system dynamics modeling has been applied specifically to cancer prevention and control has not been studied.
elements.reason: The Introduction explains the need for the review by citing calls for systems science approaches in cancer control and the unexamined extent of system dynamics application to cancer prevention and control.

elements.quote: Although system dynamics modeling has been utilized in various aspects of public health since the 1970s, past reviews in this field have noted a significant increase in their use since the early 2000s... The extent to which system dynamics modeling has been applied specifically to cancer prevention and control has not been studied.
elements.reason: The manuscript indicates no prior similar systematic review specific to cancer prevention and control exists, so the conditional requirement to cite and differentiate from previous reviews does not apply.
This is a methods review of system dynamics modeling applications, not a review of intervention effects, so describing an intervention mechanism of action does not apply.
